findings.title: Catalog limit rejection does not poison the journal instance
findings.evidence: At max frame count or when the next frame would exceed max bytes, Transition returns errPilotCatalogLimit without setting journal.poisoned. Subsequent Snapshot and other-case transitions remain usable, contrary to §109's global fail-closed limit behavior.
findings.recommendation: Poison the journal/supervisor on catalog-wide capacity exhaustion and add tests that subsequent snapshot/transition calls fail closed after either cap is reached.

findings.title: Transition file Sync failure is not directly tested
findings.evidence: Sync errors are injected for first-frame creation and startup replay, but not after a normal transition frame has been appended.
findings.recommendation: Inject Transition Sync failure; assert error, poison, no same-instance retry, and restart behavior according to complete-valid-frame authority.

findings.title: In-memory lock concurrency and framing corruption do not satisfy child-process/canonical JSON acceptance
findings.evidence: The generation test uses a fake mutex lock; the platform lock test is sequential on one handle. Current malformed tests focus framing corruption and do not explicitly lock duplicate/unknown/trailing/noncanonical JSON payload behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add child-process writers with independently opened verified lock handles and explicit canonical payload negative vectors as required by §109.4.

passed_checks: CRC-32C frame encoding/decoding, duplicate-length/trailer validation, canonical re-encode comparison.
Replay generation continuity, per-case state transitions, and no case-ID reuse.
Startup replay and file/parent Sync occur while global lock is held.
First provisioning frame is exclusive-bootstrap supplied, written and synced before parent sync.
Normal append short-write, seek/stat/write/sync/unlock errors poison the journal.
scope_note: Path, ACL, identity, bootstrap lock, and real supervisor behavior are outside these two files and remain integration gates.
